sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-PA antibody detection confirmed expression of the tagged construct in skeletal muscle; no functional assay result reported in the clip for the WT-PA construct specifically.
sites.rationale: LSMEM2 is a single-pass membrane protein with its sole extracellular face at the C-terminus (residues 119–164, 46 residues beyond the TM boundary at 118). The clip reports a PA-tag fusion of full-length LSMEM2 detected by anti-PA antibody in muscle, confirming surface accessibility of the tag. Because no junction residue is named and exactly one terminus is extracellular, the position is topology-derived at residue 164 (S). Python confirmed residue 164 = S, no cysteines in the extracellular domain, and 46-residue clearance from the TM boundary. Full-length LSMEM2 WT expressed via AAV in skeletal muscle as a C-terminal PA-tag fusion (GVAMPGAEDDVV); detected by anti-PA antibody. The clip names no junction residue. LSMEM2 has a single TM (98–118) with an intracellular N-terminus (1–97) and an extracellular C-terminus (119–164); exactly one terminus is extracellular, placing the tag after residue 164 by topology.

sources.claim: LSMEM2 WT and C‐del (deleted from aa110 [Serine] to 150 [C‐terminus]) fused with PA tag (GVAMPGAEDDVV) [ 13 ].

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is available. It supports a single C-terminal PA-tag site on the extracellular face. The C-del mutant (deletion of ~aa110–150) described in the same clip is a truncation construct whose PA tag, if C-terminal, would reside in the TM or intracellular region and does not constitute a surface tag site. The N-terminus (residue 1) is intracellular and was not considered. No internal extracellular loop insertions are supported by the ledger. A potential N-glycosylation sequon (N156-S157-S158) exists 8 residues from the C-terminus but is not at the tag junction and does not affect the terminal site.
